result.question: Why do leprous men go to Arameans?

readings.answer: To have a chance to live
readings.support: let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they let us live, we will live

readings.answer: Because they would die in the city from the famine
readings.support: we will die there from the famine in the city

readings.answer: Because staying where they are also means death
readings.support: but if we sit here, we will also die

assessments.reason: The text says, “let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they let us live, we will live,” which is a complementary motive to the key’s focus on death if they stay.
“We will die there from the famine in the city” is another stated reason for choosing the Arameans, consistent with but not identical to the key’s emphasis on staying leading to death.
“But if we sit here, we will also die” directly matches the key’s idea that staying means they might die.
